about: Launch vehicles that carry CLPS landers. Weather limits are in weather_rules; a limit no vehicle maker publishes is entered by the team, never filled in here. Injection accuracy is what a vehicle's own user guide prints, row by row, with the page in the source's title; a guide with none has none here.

records.name: Falcon 9 Block 5

injection_accuracy.orbit: LEO direct inject (200 km x 360 km)
injection_accuracy.cited: Falcon 9 Launch Vehicle Payload User’s Guide, Rev 2 (21 October 2015), Table 3-2, page 16
injection_accuracy.note: The guide prints no argument of perigee for it (N/A). Its footnote 2: the RAAN figure assumes an instantaneous launch window, a nonstandard service; for the standard one-hour window the RAAN is about 7.5 degrees, set by the launch time.

injection_accuracy.orbit: Geosynchronous transfer orbit (185 km x 35,786 km)
injection_accuracy.cited: Falcon 9 Launch Vehicle Payload User’s Guide, Rev 2 (21 October 2015), Table 3-2, page 16
injection_accuracy.note: RAAN as in the row above (footnote 2 of the table).

sources.title: Launch Library 2: upcoming launches at Kennedy, Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg (booster landing plans per launch)

Falcon 9 Launch Vehicle Payload User's Guide, Rev 2 (21 October 2015), section 3.6 Orbit Insertion Accuracy, Table 3-2, page 16 of 69: accuracies at 3 sigma for the osculating elements at orbit insertion (SpaceX's file, as archived on 23 December 2016; SHA-256 a47b5ea023db7f094052596887c3f35010f5a808b348a882193509167f2e6ae0)

notes: Launch Library 2 lists droneship (ASDS) and land (RTLS) booster landings for upcoming Falcon 9 flights.

Only Rev 2 (October 2015) of SpaceX's Falcon guide prints an orbit-insertion accuracy: the guides of April 2020, September 2021 and May 2025 were read and have none (they give a separation attitude and its accuracy only), so this is the accuracy the guide gave for the vehicle of 2015, not a figure for Block 5.

injection_sigma.reason: The guide does not say how many standard deviations the plus-or-minus of its table stands for (it calls the table predicted guidance accuracy). Three is what the Falcon 9 and New Glenn guides print for theirs and the usual convention; if it were one, every error taken from the table would be three times larger.

notes: Launch Library 2 lists no booster landing for Vulcan flights.
The table's kilometre values are the guide's first figures; its nautical miles are in brackets beside them.

injection_accuracy.orbit: LEO: apogee and perigee altitude at least 200 km, inclination 28 to 51.6 degrees
injection_accuracy.cited: New Glenn Payload User’s Guide, Rev C (October 2018), Table 2-3, page 31
injection_accuracy.note: The guide prints the argument of perigee as (circular) and the altitudes as at least 200 km.

injection_accuracy.orbit: GTO: apogee altitude 35,786 km, perigee altitude at least 185 km, inclination 27 degrees or less
injection_accuracy.cited: New Glenn Payload User’s Guide, Rev C (October 2018), Table 2-3, page 31
injection_accuracy.note: The guide prints the perigee altitude as at least 185 km; 185 km is taken as the reference orbit's perigee, the standard GTO's.

notes: LC-36, New Glenn's only pad, was damaged on 28 May 2026 (see launch_sites).
Blue Origin says it is designing New Glenn to achieve these accuracies (the vehicle had not yet flown when the guide was written, in 2018).
